previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis, chronic opiate use, and asthma was admitted for abdominal pain and shortness of breath after resuming alcohol use. He was treated for alcohol withdrawal with Ativan taper, managed for an asthma exacerbation with steroids and antibiotics, and evaluated for abdominal pain, which was attributed to alcoholic gastritis after a CT scan showed no acute pathology. His methadone was continued, and he was stabilized on supportive care. Liver enzymes showed mild elevation with a downtrend. He improved clinically, was discharged home with a short course of pain medication, and advised to follow up for an EGD and substance use counseling.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ y/o male with a history of ETOH cirrhosis, pancreatitis, ETOH 
withdrawal seizures, substance abuse on methadone, and asthma 
requiring intubations who presented with several days of 
abdominal pain, blood streaked emesis and dark stools, briefly 
requiring MICU admission given concern for GI bleed, course 
complicated by protracted EtOH withdrawal course, and chronic 
abdominal pain and anxiety.

#Gastrointestinal bleed: 
On admission, the patient reported several days of abdominal 
pain, blood streaked emesis and dark stools. Given his history 
of cirrhosis and varices on a CT scan in the past, IV PPI, 
octreotide gtt, and ceftriaxone were started. He had an EGD on 
___ that was notable for portal hypertensive gastropathy. 
Subsequently, he was switched to po PPI and octreotide was 
stopped. He had no further signs of bleeding prior to discharge, 
and was hemodynamically stable with stable blood counts. He will 
follow up with Dr. ___ in the ___ clinic for further 
management of his cirrhosis and GI bleeding. 

#Alcoholic cirrhosis, decompensated, complicated by hepatic 
encephalopathy, portal hypertensive gastropathy:
GI bleeding managed as above. He was encephalopathic on 
admission with confusion and asterixis. He improved with 
lactulose. His home dose of lactulose was increased from 15 ml 
to 30 ml TID with goal ___ bowel movements. He has not been 
previously treated for cirrhosis and will follow up with Dr. 
___ in clinic. He was previously on spironolactone and Lasix, 
which were initially held in the setting of bleeding, but 
restarted prior to discharge. He was discharged on 
spironolactone 100 mg daily instead of BID. MELD 15 on 
discharge. Currently not a transplant candidate given his recent 
alcohol use. Social work was consulted and patient declined any 
outpatient services for alcohol, as he claims that he will not 
drink anymore and he only had a brief relapse of three days of 
drinking.

#Abdominal pain: 
On admission the patient reported bilateral upper abdominal 
pain, similar to previous episodes of pancreatitis. Lipase 
normal. CT scan was done initially without contrast and showed 
possible concerning liver mass, but repeat CT with contrast 
revealed only regenerative nodules. This abdominal pain is 
likely chronic, related to expanding liver swelling with 
capsular stretching, exacerbated by the patient's ongoing 
anxiety and concurrent withdrawal during admission. His 
abdominal pain improved to a tolerable level prior to discharge 
on tramadol. We will discharge him with a few tablets of 
tramadol for abdominal pain, and he will follow up with his PCP. 
He will also continue home methadone. Additionally, he had a few 
episodes of diarrhea which slowly improved. C. diff was 
negative.

#Asthma: 
Presented with several days of shortness of breath. Reports a 
history of intermittent SOB like this at baseline. He has a 
history of asthma requiring multiple intubations in the past. He 
was treated with nebulizers and advair and tiotropium inhalers 
with improvement in symptoms. Will be discharged on home regimen 
of albuterol, tiotropiium bromide, and symbicort. 

#Anxiety/Panic attacks: 
Reports a history of episodic chest pain, SOB, and anxiety for 
the last 1.5 months. Denied being treated for this in the past. 
Psychiatry consulted and recommended outpatient management with 
psychiatric services at ___ clinic. He was initially 
treated with lorazepam especially in setting of withdrawal, but 
discharged on his home hydroxyzine. Will need outpatient 
follow-up. 

#ETOH use:
Began drinking large volumes of alcohol for three days prior to 
admission after being sober for several months. Last drink at 
02:00 on ___. Presented with tremors, nausea, vomiting, 
diarrhea, abdominal pain, concerning for possible withdrawal, 
which required multiple doses of Ativan due to scoring on the 
CIWA scale, which was likely compounded by his underlying 
anxiety. He should continue to take thiamine, folic acid, and 
multivitamin. He will follow up with the resources at his 
___ clinic regarding maintaining sobriety.

#Opiate dependence:
Long history of hydromorphone use/abuse with issues in the past 
with getting discharged from methadone clinics. Currently on 
methadone 70 mg daily, a lower daily dose than what he had been 
previously getting (75 mg) given liver failure, which he 
tolerated well.

# Elevated Transaminases: 
Mildly elevated AST, Alk phos in 700s. Has history of similar 
elevation in the past with elevated gtt to the thousands. MRCP 
done in ___ showed no duct dilations or masses. Monitored 
while inpatient. Likely a component of alcoholic hepatitis.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CT abdomen pelvis with contrast

INDICATION:  ___ male with h/o cirrhosis p/w severe abdominal pain
with generalized ttp.  Acute intra-abdominal process to explain pain.

TECHNIQUE:  Single phase split bolus contrast: MDCT axial images were acquired
through the abdomen and pelvis following intravenous contrast administration
with split bolus technique.
Oral contrast was not administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Stationary Acquisition 5.5 s, 0.5 cm; CTDIvol = 26.5 mGy (Body) DLP =
13.2 mGy-cm.
   2) Spiral Acquisition 4.5 s, 48.9 cm; CTDIvol = 16.8 mGy (Body) DLP = 823.4
mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 837 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen pelvis from ___.

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST: There is mild right lower lobe atelectasis.  Otherwise,
visualized lung fields are within normal limits. There is no evidence of
pleural or pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver is nodular in contour.  The left lobe of the liver
and the caudate are hypertrophic with mild atrophy of the right lobe of the
liver, consistent with cirrhotic morphology.  There is a patent umbilical
vein.  There is a subtle 1.2 cm hypodensity in hepatic segment 3 (02:29),
which appears to be new since ___. There is no evidence of
intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder is partially
collapsed.  The gallbladder wall is slightly edematous, likely related to
underlying liver disease.

PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic
stranding.

SPLEEN: The spleen is stably enlarged, measuring 16.2 cm, displacing the left
kidney inferiorly..  No focal lesion is seen.

ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY: The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
There is no evidence of focal renal lesions or hydronephrosis.  There is no
perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL: The stomach is unremarkable.  Small bowel loops demonstrate
normal caliber, wall thickness, and enhancement throughout.  The colon and
rectum are within normal limits.  The appendix is normal (02:54).

PELVIS: The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: The prostate and seminal vesicles are unremarkable.

LYMPH NODES: There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR: There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  Mild atherosclerotic disease
is noted.  Extensive paraesophageal, perigastric and perisplenic varices are
again noted.  The the umbilical vein is recannulized.

BONES: There is mild degenerative changes of the lumbar spine.  There is no
evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture.

SOFT TISSUES: The abdominal and pelvic wall is within normal limits.

IMPRESSION:


1. 1.2 cm hypodensity in hepatic segment 3 of the liver, likely new since ___.  Given hepatic cirrhosis, further evaluation with a
nonemergent multiphasic liver CT or MRI is recommended.
2. No acute intra-abdominal or intrapelvic abnormalities.
3. Cirrhotic morphology with evidence portal hypertension, including
splenomegaly and extensive parasagittal, perigastric and perisplenic varices.

EXAMINATION:  CHEST (PORTABLE AP)

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with ETOH cirrhosis, asthma, having some
increased shortness of breath, decreased breath sounds at the right base.//
Concern for pleural effusion     Concern for pleural effusion

IMPRESSION: 

Heart size and mediastinum are stable.  Lungs are clear.  There is no pleural
effusion.  There is no pneumothorax.

EXAMINATION:  CT abdomen with IV contrast.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with EtOH cirrhosis, found to have 1.3 cm mass on
CT noncontrast.// Better evaluation of liver mass with multiphasic CT scan

TECHNIQUE:  Multiphasic Liver: Multidetector CT of the abdomen was performed
without and with IV contrast. Initially, the abdomen was scanned without IV
contrast. Subsequently, a single bolus of IV contrast was injected and the
abdomen was scanned in the early arterial phase, followed by a scan of the
abdomen in the portal venous phase, followed by a scan of the abdomen in
equilibrium phase (3-min delay).
Oral contrast was not administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:  Total DLP (Body) = 1,978 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST: Atelectasis, but no focal consolidations.  No pleural or
pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver is cirrhotic in appearance.  There is a 1.3 x 0.9 cm
hypoenhancing lesion within the left lobe of the liver (series 3, image 52). 
This lesion appears to be hypoenhancing on all phases, and likely represents a
regenerative nodule.  An additional adjacent punctate hypodensity within the
left lobe of the liver is also new (series 3, image 45), also likely a
regenerative nodule.  There are no enhancing lesions demonstrating washout. 
There is no evidence of intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The
gallbladder is within normal limits.  Patent paraumbilical vein.  Numerous
perisplenic varices are visualized including a splenorenal shunt. No ascites.

PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic
stranding.

SPLEEN: The spleen is enlarged measuring 16.6 cm.  No focal splenic lesions.

ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY: The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
There is no evidence of focal renal lesions or hydronephrosis.  There is no
perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL: The stomach is unremarkable.  The visualized small and large
bowel are also unremarkable in appearance.

LYMPH NODES: There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR: There is no visualized abdominal aortic aneurysm.  Mild
atherosclerotic disease is noted.

BONES: Chronic appearing fracture of the right anterior rib (series 2, image
12).  Compression deformities to the superior endplates of T7 and T9 with mild
height loss is unchanged since at least ___.  There is no evidence of
worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture.

SOFT TISSUES: Subcutaneous air and nodularity within the anterior abdominal
wall is likely due to injections.

IMPRESSION:


1. Cirrhotic appearing liver.  No lesions concerning for HCC.
2. 2 new hypoenhancing lesions within left lobe of the liver measuring up to
1.3 cm, consistent with regenerative nodules.
3. Sequela of portal hypertension include a patent paraumbilical vein,
numerous varices, and splenomegaly.  No ascites.
